newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says 31 people slaughtered near capital.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says 31 people slaughtered near capital.

text.p: Moslem fundamentalists killed 31 people in an attack near Blida, south of the Algerian capital, between Tuesday night and Wednesday morning, Algerian security forces said.
A statement, carried by the official Algerian news agency APS, said the 31 had been "assassinated in a cowardly way" in what it described as "this ignoble terrorist act".
Algeria uses the term "terrorist" to describe Moslem guerrillas who have been fighting to topple the government.
The killing was the second mass murder within three days, following the slaying of 10 women and three children -- all with their throats cut -- on Saturday night.
The 31 who died in the latest attack blamed on fundamentalists were killed in the village of Sid el Kebir on the road to Chrea in Blida province, which lies some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
